target: ArrayApp (.NET 10 WebAPI / EF Core / Identity / Angular)

findings.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) Leading to Complete Account Takeover
findings.description: The ResetPassword endpoint accepted a target user's Email address and a new password with an unauthenticated [AllowAnonymous] policy and without validating a cryptographic password reset token or authenticating caller ownership. Any external adversary could reset any user's password (including Administrator) by supplying their email.
findings.businessImpact: Immediate total compromise of application administrator accounts and all tenant accounts, leading to uninhibited data exfiltration, regulatory penalties (GDPR/HIPAA/SOC2), and severe brand damage.
findings.remediationSummary: Restructured endpoint to validate caller authentication, verify ownership or identity reset token via ASP.NET Identity UserManager.ResetPasswordAsync, or verify current password via ChangePasswordAsync. Added ResetToken and CurrentPassword to ResetPasswordModel.

findings.title: Vertical Privilege Escalation and Missing Functional Authorization on RBAC Endpoints
findings.description: Administrative role management endpoints lacked authorization attributes, allowing any anonymous unauthenticated network client to create arbitrary roles and grant themselves or any other user administrative privileges.
findings.businessImpact: Any attacker could instantly grant themselves the Administrator role, subverting all role-based security boundaries across the enterprise system.
findings.remediationSummary: Enforced strict role-based authorization attributes: [Authorize(Roles = "Administrator,Admin,admin")] across all role creation, assignment, deletion, and user query endpoints.

findings.title: Broad Attack Surface from Missing Authentication Across 35 API Controllers
findings.affectedEndpoint: 35 Core Controllers (Campaigns, Products, Innovation, Connectors, AI Agents, ZeroTrust, Compliance, etc.)
findings.description: 35 out of 38 WebAPI controllers lacked the [Authorize] attribute at the class and action levels. Unauthenticated internet clients had full read, create, update, and delete access to business data, enterprise strategy, chatrooms, and compliance logs.
findings.businessImpact: Total disclosure of proprietary business data, campaign strategies, financial metrics, and customer communications; unauthorized manipulation and tampering with corporate assets.
findings.remediationSummary: Applied explicit [Authorize] attributes to all 35 controllers and made BaseController abstract. System adheres to secure-by-default zero trust posture.

findings.title: Mass Sensitive Data Exposure via Password Hash and Security Stamp Leaks
findings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.owaspCategory: API3:2023 - Broken Object Property Level Authorization
findings.description: User queries directly serialized ASP.NET Identity ApplicationUser domain entities into JSON HTTP responses, exposing PasswordHash (PBKDF2/Argon2 hashes), SecurityStamp, ConcurrencyStamp, and internal system flags.
findings.businessImpact: Adversaries could scrape password hashes across all accounts for offline dictionary/GPU cracking attacks, and security stamps could be abused to forge or invalidate authentication states.
findings.remediationSummary: Introduced UserDto projection model in Application layer that strictly encapsulates safe public profile fields (Id, UserName, Email, PhoneNumber, etc.) and completely omits cryptographic hashes, stamps, and tokens.

findings.title: Exception Stack Trace and Internal Path Leakage in Error Responses
findings.cweName: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
findings.affectedEndpoint: Over 29 API action catch blocks and global error filters
findings.description: Catch blocks in IdeaController and FileDataController explicitly formatted and returned `ex.StackTrace` and internal filesystem paths in HTTP 500 error responses.
findings.businessImpact: Provides attackers with complete internal architecture maps, exact source code line numbers, server file paths, third-party libraries, and database ORM call sequences.
findings.remediationSummary: Removed all 29 instances of ex.StackTrace disclosure. Sanitized ApiExceptionFilterAttribute in both WebAPI and WebUI to produce RFC 7807 compliant ProblemDetails with opaque correlation traceId.

findings.title: Weak Cryptographic Key Length (128-bit) and Inadequate JWT Signature Validation
findings.description: JWT authentication used a hardcoded 16-character (128-bit) secret key `C421AAEE0D114E9C`, violating NIST SP 800-131A and RFC 7518 HMAC-SHA256 requirements. Token validation also failed to enforce audience validation.
findings.businessImpact: Vulnerable to offline brute force and rainbow table recovery. Allows adversaries to forge arbitrary JWT tokens with any identity and roles.
findings.remediationSummary: Upgraded JWT validation to mandate a cryptographically secure 256-bit+ key, enforced ValidateIssuer, ValidateAudience, ValidateLifetime, and ClockSkew = Zero. Replaced static 128-bit strings with 256-bit configuration template.

findings.title: Missing Rate Limiting and Brute-Force Lockout on Authentication Endpoints
findings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
findings.description: Authentication endpoints lacked request throttling, IP rate limiting, and Identity account lockout mechanisms. Attackers could execute credential stuffing and brute-force dictionary attacks unhindered.
findings.businessImpact: Account compromise via automated credential spraying, credential stuffing, and denial-of-service against the Identity backend.
findings.remediationSummary: Enabled ASP.NET Core RateLimiter middleware with strict fixed-window policy (10 requests/minute on auth endpoints, 100 requests/minute on global API). Configured ASP.NET Identity lockout with MaxFailedAccessAttempts = 5 and DefaultLockoutTimeSpan = 15m. Added AccessFailedAsync tracking in TokenController.

findings.title: Client-Controlled ABAC Attributes and Privilege Escalation in Zero Trust Governance
findings.description: ZeroTrustGovernanceController allowed callers to pass arbitrary clearance levels, roles, and trust scores as unauthenticated query parameters. The access evaluation engine relied on client-supplied parameters rather than validated server-side claims.
findings.businessImpact: Any user could bypass ABAC governance controls and access Top Secret or Compartmentalized enterprise assets simply by appending `userClearance=TopSecret` to the query string.
findings.remediationSummary: Added [Authorize] to controller and rebound user clearance, user roles, and device trust evaluation to cryptographically signed claims from the validated ClaimsPrincipal.

findings.title: Container Security: End-of-Life .NET 7 Base Image, Root Execution, and Missing Health Checks
findings.description: Dockerfile used out-of-support .NET 7 base images (`mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:7.0`), executed container processes as root (UID 0), exposed privileged port 80, and lacked container healthcheck directives.
findings.businessImpact: Container breakout risks from unpatched OS/runtime CVEs, and potential root host compromise if container isolation is breached.
findings.remediationSummary: Upgraded base images to .NET 10 LTS (`mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0`), created and switched to non-root user `appuser:appgroup` (UID 10001), shifted listening port to unprivileged 8080, and configured container HEALTHCHECK.
findings.verificationTest: Automated verification in infrastructure-container-audit.md and Dockerfile inspection

findings.title: Hardcoded Database Credentials and Deprecated Runners in CI/CD Workflows
findings.description: GitHub Actions workflows contained hardcoded SQL Server SA passwords (`Your_password123`), utilized obsolete action versions (`actions/checkout@v2`, `upload-artifact@v2`), and relied on vulnerable deprecated `::set-output` syntax.
findings.businessImpact: Credential exposure in workflow logs and build history; susceptibility to workflow injection and supply chain compromise from unmaintained action dependencies.
findings.remediationSummary: Extracted SA passwords to GitHub Actions Secrets `${{ secrets.SQL_SA_PASSWORD }}`, upgraded all actions to current major versions (v4/v3), and updated output syntax to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
findings.verificationTest: Automated syntax and secrets validation in CI/CD workflows

findings.title: Permissive Password Policy Allowing Trivial and Weak Credentials
findings.description: Default Identity setup allowed passwords with length down to 6 characters and lacked requirements for uppercase letters, digits, and special characters, allowing weak passwords vulnerable to rapid guessing.
findings.businessImpact: Vulnerability to automated dictionary attacks and offline hash cracking if hashes are ever intercepted.
findings.remediationSummary: Configured strict password complexity: RequiredLength = 8, RequireDigit = true, RequireUppercase = true, RequireLowercase = true, RequireNonAlphanumeric = true, RequiredUniqueChars = 4.

findings.title: Missing Security Response Headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy)
findings.description: WebAPI did not emit modern defensive HTTP headers, leaving clients exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing attacks, and cross-site scripting risks.
findings.businessImpact: Vulnerability to UI redressing (clickjacking), downgrade attacks, and speculative execution side-channel leaks.
findings.remediationSummary: Added custom security headers middleware to Program.cs injecting Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Permissions-Policy.
findings.verificationTest: Pipeline middleware inspection and unit test validation

findings.title: Excessive JWT Token Validity Duration (50 Hours)
findings.description: appsettings configured JWT token expiration to 180,000 seconds (50 hours), keeping compromised tokens valid for over two days with no active revocation mechanism.
findings.businessImpact: Prolonged attacker persistence following credential compromise or token theft via XSS/man-in-the-browser.
findings.remediationSummary: Reduced JWT token duration to 3,600 seconds (1 hour) in appsettings configuration, minimizing the blast radius and window of vulnerability.
findings.verificationTest: Configuration file audit and token lifetime validation

findings.title: Sync-Over-Async Thread Pool Starvation Hazard in Account Controller
findings.description: AccountController used `_userManager.GetUsersInRoleAsync(roleName).Result`, blocking asynchronous thread pool threads during synchronous waiting.
findings.businessImpact: Thread pool starvation and unresponsiveness (Denial of Service) under moderate concurrent traffic loads.
findings.remediationSummary: Refactored GetUsersInRole and related methods to pure async/await patterns using `await _userManager.GetUsersInRoleAsync(roleName)`.
findings.verificationTest: Code review and async compilation verification

findings.title: Unencrypted Database Connection String Defaults
findings.description: Connection strings did not enforce TLS transport encryption (`Encrypt=true`), enabling potential eavesdropping on unencrypted internal database network traffic.
findings.businessImpact: Interception of plaintext SQL queries, customer PII, and credentials on unsegmented internal networks.
findings.remediationSummary: Appended `Encrypt=true;TrustServerCertificate=true;` to all development and default database connection strings.

findings.title: Verbosity of Production Logging Defaults to Debug Level
findings.cweName: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
findings.description: appsettings.Production.json configured default logging level to `Debug`, increasing log volume, storage costs, and risk of inadvertent PII ingestion.
findings.businessImpact: Excessive log storage consumption, performance degradation, and accidental logging of request payloads containing sensitive data.
findings.remediationSummary: Modified `Default` logging level in appsettings.Production.json to `Warning`, preserving critical alerts while suppressing debug telemetry.

findings.title: Secret Sprawl in Source Control History and Local appsettings Files
findings.affectedComponent: Git Commit History & Repository Configuration Files
findings.description: Historic commits contain development secrets (128-bit JWT test keys, default SA passwords). While code files have been remediated with strong placeholder keys, Git commit history retains historical artifacts.
findings.businessImpact: Any party with clone access to the historical git graph can extract historical test passwords and symmetric keys.
findings.remediationSummary: All source files have been scrubbed. Production environments must inject secrets via Azure Key Vault or AWS Secrets Manager. Development teams must rotate any real credentials and consider BFG Repo-Cleaner / git-filter-repo if repo is made public.
findings.verificationTest: Git history audit documented in secrets-audit.md
